questions.prompt: What implementation scope should this goal treat as required before it can be marked complete?
questions.description: The source docs describe a full Cloudflare-first business operating system. The grill settled that milestones are allowed, but completion should remain full end-to-end delivery.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require all core Dawn slices from the authoritative docs: ADR baseline, team/permissions, domain/app layers, Postgres/Drizzle authoritative data, audit/idempotency/outbox, ledger, CSV/banking sync, documents/R2/inbox/extraction/matching, invoicing/payments/recurrence, projects/time tracking, reports/insights, TanStack DB sync/realtime, TanStack AI assistant/tools/approval/evals, automations, integrations, public API/webhooks, desktop improvements, observability, operations, and production gates. Allow milestone commits, but do not mark complete while required slices remain incomplete.

questions.prompt: How autonomous should the orchestrator be while executing the goal?
questions.description: This determines when the orchestrator should stop for user input versus continuing through worker spawning, merges, verification, docs, and commits.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use high autonomy inside the documented architecture. The orchestrator may create branches/worktrees, spawn Codex CLI workers, review and merge output, update ADRs/docs, and commit verified units. Stop only for product scope changes, architecture non-negotiable conflicts, credential/deployment needs, or risk to user changes.

questions.prompt: What architecture posture should workers follow when implementation touches starter code or transitional paths?
questions.description: The user requested zero tech debt during grilling.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a zero-tech-debt posture. Build as if the intended architecture existed from day one: business rules in packages/domain and packages/app, thin transports, final product names, no speculative compatibility wrappers, and removal of unused starter paths when caller evidence supports deletion. Preserve only real external contracts, persisted data, or explicit product requirements.

questions.prompt: How should the goal handle live services and credentials that may not be available locally?
questions.description: Examples include banking providers, email, payments, R2, Queues, Workflows, AI APIs, public webhooks, and Cloudflare deploy.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Implement provider boundaries, local/test adapters, schemas, use cases, verification harnesses, signed webhook fixtures, and production binding docs first. Mark only live credential-dependent or deployed-infrastructure wiring as blocked when actual secrets, accounts, or deployments are required.

questions.prompt: What must be true before a worker result can be merged or a milestone can be committed?
questions.description: This should become the quality gate for the orchestrator and any spawned workers.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require diff inspection, acceptance criteria verification, relevant checks, docs/ADR updates when behavior or decisions changed, and orchestration tracking before every merge or commit. Partial commits are allowed only when independently useful, verified, documented as partial, and not a regression for future slices.
